tools.name: get_account_status
tools.description: What stands between you and a live pay link: whether the owner's email is confirmed, the receiving-address policy, how many addresses are approved or waiting for approval, unsettled fees, your key's scopes, and the next steps. Requires scope drafts:read.

findings.detail: Description of "create_account" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_transaction_template, get_account_status, create_account · Private data: get_transaction_template, propose_receiving_address, submit_lightning_proof, create_account, get_rate, create_draft · Public sink: propose_receiving_address, get_account_status, submit_lightning_proof, create_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_transaction_template, get_account_status, create_account · Private data: get_transaction_template, propose_receiving_address, submit_lightning_proof, create_account, get_rate, create_draft · Public sink: propose_receiving_address, get_account_status, submit_lightning_proof, create_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_transaction_template" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
